Hi Sarah — great questions. Short answers up front, then details and action items below.

Summary:
- We can minimize VPC peering; the control plane (for Private customers) will use a private endpoint model where possible. The inference fleet for on-prem appliances will require a bi-directional peering or dedicated egress route for telemetry/backups if you want managed metrics/patching.
- CIDRs: see suggested ranges below; we can be flexible but need non-overlapping blocks.
- On-prem package: we support air-gapped installs with a staging USB bundle and an offline license token.

Suggested CIDRs and ports (proposal):
- Redwood managed endpoint (s-priv-01): 10.240.32.0/27 (peering or BGP)
- Appliance management plane (if using peering): 10.240.33.0/28
- Customer private endpoint NAT egress: source NAT from 172.20.0.0/20
- Ports: 443 (API), 5222 (optional control), 9000-9100 (inter-node heartbeats, if appliance)

Action items:
1) Confirm whether NorthForge wants fully managed telemetry (requires peering) or isolated offline mode (air-gapped).
2) If peering chosen: provide your preferred non-overlapping VPC CIDR for peering and your firewall contact for route propagation.
3) If air-gapped: we’ll send package checklist + staging USB manifest and the offline license token process.

Proposed preflight slots: Tue 2026-09-15 09:00-10:00 PT or Thu 2026-09-17 13:00-14:00 PT. I’ll block Tue for now and we can move if needed.

I’ve attached our internal onprem checklist and a peering template.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-onprem-checklist-v0.9.xlsx; vpc-peering-template.txt

Looping in a few details from infra:

- For managed telemetry we typically prefer a single /27 to keep route table entries minimal. If NorthForge wants BGP, we support a short-lived BGP session (we’ll provide ASN prep).
- For private endpoints (no peering): the recommended flow is to create an interface endpoint in the customer VPC that points to the Redwood Private control plane. This avoids long-lived peering but requires internal ALB + NLB configuration on your side.

Notes on firewall rules (customer-facing):
- Outbound to Redwood control plane: 10.240.32.0/27 TCP 443
- Outbound to telemetry bucket (if enabled): 52.84.120.0/22 TCP 443 (we’ll support IP ranges per region)

I’ll draft the BGP and peering notes into INF-1428 and link the runbook.

Dylan
